LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 EXTENSIVE LISTENING: ● LISTENING FOR ENJOYMENT ● LISTENING FOR GENERAL UNDERSTANDING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Listening and Speaking ● Extensive listening ● Etiquette ● Critical listening ● 
Topic 1.1: listening and speaking 1.1.1 extensive listening: ● listening for enjoyment ● listening for general understanding
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers listening and speaking 1.1.1 extensive listening: ● listening for enjoyment ● listening for general understanding, part of Listening and Speaking ● Extensive listening ● Etiquette ● Critical listening ●  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: how can one identify main ideas in an oral text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe characters, places and memorable events from a recording,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of listening and speaking 1.1.1 extensive listening: ● listening for enjoyment ● listening for general understanding in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. listen to a recording and pick key details for general information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of listening and speaking 1.1.1 extensive listening: ● listening for enjoyment ● listening for general understanding in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. interact with a wide range of oral texts for general understanding and enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of listening and speaking 1.1.1 extensive listening: ● listening for enjoyment ● listening for general understanding in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. recount a story or dialogue in an oral context for enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of listening and speaking 1.1.1 extensive listening: ● listening for enjoyment ● listening for general understanding in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. acknowledge the role of identifying key information for lifelong learning. ● in groups, learners are guided to listen to recordings from contexts such as role plays and skits and then recount the characters, places and memorable events, ● in groups,learners are guided in a hot seating session based on a dialogue or story and recount characters, places and events, ● in pairs, learners are guided to listen to a telephone conversation and pick key details, how can one identify main ideas in an oral text? 2 ● in groups, learners are guided to mimic a character in a story or in a dialogue, ● in pairs, learners are guided to listen to and dramatise a dialogue between a hotel attendant and a customer in groups, ● in groups or in pairs, learners with low vision are guided to watch videos while learners with blindness listen to audio clips using digital devices with assistive technology on table etiquette and jointly re- enact it, ● in pairs, learners are guided to record a dialogue on etiquette and upload it on an online platform.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on listening and speaking 1.1.1 extensive listening: ● listening for enjoyment ● listening for general understanding together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● creativity and imagination: the learner gains new perspectives on hotel etiquette as they dramatise the dialogue between a

hotel attendant and a customer.

● digital literacy: the learner uses digital devices with assistive technology to record a narration or dialogue and uploads it on

online platforms.

3

Values:
● Unity: The learner displays team spirit as they work with others to role play events in the story or dialogue.

● Responsibility: The learner displays responsibility as they manipulate digital devices with assistive technology.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Developmental perspective: The learner learns about healthy relationships as they watch or listen to a clip on table etiquette.

● Print texts

● Braille texts

● Electronic reading materials

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Main points to remember:

1. describe characters, places and memorable events from a recording,
2. listen to a recording and pick key details for general information,
3. interact with a wide range of oral texts for general understanding and enjoyment,
4. recount a story or dialogue in an oral context for enjoyment,
5. acknowledge the role of identifying key information for lifelong learning. ● in groups, learners are guided to listen to recordings from contexts such as role plays and skits and then recount the characters, places and memorable events, ● in groups,learners are guided in a hot seating session based on a dialogue or story and recount characters, places and events, ● in pairs, learners are guided to listen to a telephone conversation and pick key details, how can one identify main ideas in an oral text? 2 ● in groups, learners are guided to mimic a character in a story or in a dialogue, ● in pairs, learners are guided to listen to and dramatise a dialogue between a hotel attendant and a customer in groups, ● in groups or in pairs, learners with low vision are guided to watch videos while learners with blindness listen to audio clips using digital devices with assistive technology on table etiquette and jointly re- enact it, ● in pairs, learners are guided to record a dialogue on etiquette and upload it on an online platform.
